title: Sandwich variance and misspecification
dek: If the mean model is right and the variance model is not, the MLE (or estimating equation) can still be consistent. The bread of the sandwich repairs the SE.
story: Maximum likelihood SEs from I(θ̂)⁻¹ believe the whole f, including Var(Y | x). Quasi-likelihood and sandwich SEs believe less. The estimating equation (the score) can have mean zero under a weaker model than the one that produced the information matrix.

Huber–White: Var(θ̂) ≈ B⁻¹ M B⁻¹, where B is the expected derivative of the score (the bread) and M is the covariance of the score (the meat). If the model is true, M = B = I and the sandwich collapses to I⁻¹. If not, it does not.

Cluster-robust meat sums scores within district or household before taking outer products. That is often the minimum adult SE in a TB survey even when you refuse a full mixed model. It does not fix a wrong mean: omitted confounding still biases β̂.
deepTitle: What is consistent, and what is not a test
deep: Consistency target: the solution of E[S(θ)] = 0. For a GLM, that is often the coefficient of a correctly specified mean g(E[Y|x]) = xᵀβ, even if V(μ) is wrong. For a misspecified mean, sandwich SEs are honest about noise around the wrong functional.

Do not mix a model-based LRT (which uses the full likelihood, including V) with sandwich SEs and call them one test. Wald with sandwich covariance is the matching robust test. Likelihood-ratio χ² is not sandwich-aware.

Finite-sample sandwiches can be liberal with few clusters. With 8 labs, a bias-reduced or clustered bootstrap SE is often more trustworthy than HC0. Report the number of clusters next to the robust SE.

In WGS association, sandwich-on-individuals still assumes the estimating equation is unbiased. Population structure that shifts both genotype and phenotype is a mean-model failure; a sandwich will not save you — see the GWAS plates.

formulas.label: Sandwich covariance
formulas.note: B = −∑ ∂Sᵢ/∂θᵀ, M = ∑ Sᵢ Sᵢᵀ (or clustered sums). HC0/HC1/HC3 are small-sample variants of M.

formulas.label: Estimating equation
formulas.note: Mean-zero scores, not a fully believed density, are enough for consistency of θ̂.

visual.caption: Two layers of belief. Inner: mean model (what sandwich can still estimate). Outer: full exponential-family variance (what model-based I(θ) trusts). The meat of the sandwich lives in the gap between score covariance and model information.

example.title: Overdispersed clinic counts
example.setup: Weekly smear-positive counts modelled as Poisson(λᵢ) with log λᵢ = β₀ + β_rain rainᵢ. Residual deviance / df ≈ 3.2. Model-based se(β_rain) = 0.10.

steps.title: Mean may still be fine
steps.body: Rain might log-linearly shift the mean. Extra-Poisson variance (outbreaks, reporting) inflates Var(Y) above λ.

steps.title: Sandwich
steps.body: The meat M is larger than I. A sandwich se might read 0.18. The point estimate β̂_rain need not move much if the mean is right.

steps.title: Matching test
steps.body: Quote a sandwich Wald. Do not keep the Poisson LRT p-value and the sandwich SE in one sentence as if they were the same uncertainty.

example.takeaway: Sandwich is honesty about variance, not a spell against a wrong mean.

check.prompt: A sandwich SE around a GLM coefficient is most defensible when:
choices: The mean model is plausible and you distrust V(μ) or independence
The mean is known to be wrong; sandwich removes confounding
You want an LRT that uses robust variance
check.answer: The mean model is plausible and you distrust V(μ) or independence
check.why: That is the quasi-likelihood/sandwich contract. Confounding is a mean failure.

whyWrong.You want an LRT that uses robust varianc: LRT is model-based; use a robust Wald or a working bootstrap.
whyWrong.n < 10 always: Few clusters make sandwiches liberal, not automatically correct.

check.prompt: If the GLM is correctly specified, the sandwich covariance should be close to I(θ̂)⁻¹. If meat M is about 4 times I and B ≈ I, sandwich variances are about:
check.why: B⁻¹ M B⁻¹ ≈ I⁻¹ (4I) I⁻¹ = 4 I⁻¹ when B ≈ I.

check.prompt: On the nested plate, the inner box is the mean model. Why is that the inner object?
check.figureHint: Reduced: mean g(μ)=xᵀβ. Full: f including V(μ).
choices: Because sandwich consistency lives on the mean’s estimating equation, which is weaker than the full density
Because V(μ) is always estimated before the mean
Because LRTs only need the inner box
check.answer: Because sandwich consistency lives on the mean’s estimating equation, which is weaker than the full density
check.why: The geometry is belief: inner = what you need for β̂; outer = what model-based I trusts extra.
